# NVIDIA Dynamo 1.5.0 — an ALTERNATIVE serving path for Qwen3.8-27B, behind the LiteLLM router.
#
#   clients ─▶ litellm :4000 ─▶ dynamo-frontend :8000 (Rust HTTP + parsers) ─TCP─▶ dynamo-worker (vLLM 0.28.0)
#
# NOTHING EXISTING IS REWIRED. LiteLLM gets one NEW alias, `qwen3.8-27b-dynamo`, next to the
# existing `qwen3.8-27b-1m` (plain vLLM 0.27.1). Same checkpoint, same flags, so the two can be
# A/B'd through one router. Both want the same card, so they are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE:
#   scripts/use-model.sh qwen3.8-27b-dynamo     # stops vllm-qwen38, starts this
#   scripts/use-model.sh qwen3.8-27b-1m         # and back
#
# Generated 2026-09-23, unverified on a real GPU worker. What WAS checked (this image, this box):
#   - image pulled: nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/vllm-runtime:1.5.0 (20.1 GB), ai-dynamo 1.5.0,
#     vLLM 0.28.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, get_device_capability() == (12, 0) on the Workstation card
#   - every flag below appears in `--help` of dynamo.frontend / dynamo.vllm in that image
#   - the frontend<->worker plumbing across two containers: `docker compose --profile mock up`
#     (CPU-only mocker, no VRAM) — see README.md for what it proved
# Not yet checked: that the NVFP4 Qwen3.8 weights load and answer under 0.28.0 on sm_120, and the
# parser choice on real tool calls. Do that with the README's "First real run".
#
# NO etcd / NATS. Discovery is the `file` backend: frontend and worker share DYN_FILE_KV on a
# named volume; the request plane is TCP. NATS is only needed for KV-event routing, which buys
# nothing with one worker (see README).
#
# DYNAMO SPEAKS ITS OWN DIALECT ON THE WORKER, not vLLM's flags: tool/reasoning parsing runs in the
# Rust frontend and is chosen by --dyn-tool-call-parser / --dyn-reasoning-parser on the WORKER.
# Passing vLLM's --tool-call-parser here does nothing useful. Qwen3.8 uses qwen3_coder (the XML tool
# format vLLM calls qwen3_xml) — CONFIRM on a real tool call before trusting it.
#
# THE PINNED SNAPSHOT IS LOADED BY PATH, not `--model <id> --revision <sha>`. Dynamo resolves the model
# through the HF cache's refs/main, which in the lab's shared cache points at a different revision
# (f0b7c9e…, metadata only) than the pin (16b6615…, the 22 GB one). By id it crash-loops with
# "Cannot find an appropriate cached snapshot folder ... outgoing traffic has been disabled".
# Measured 2026-09-23. Same reason the mocker takes the snapshot dir.
#
# Egress: none needed. HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 — the checkpoint is already in the shared cache.
name: ai-lab-dynamo

x-image: &image nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/vllm-runtime:1.5.0
x-common: &common
  image: *image
  # Rootless Docker: uid 0 in the container is this host user, so the shared HF cache is readable.
  # The image's default uid 1000 would map to a subuid that cannot read it.
  user: "0:0"
  entrypoint: []
  networks: [ai-lab]
  cap_drop: [ALL]
  security_opt: ["no-new-privileges:true"]
  restart: unless-stopped

services:
  dynamo-frontend:
    <<: *common
    command: ["python3", "-m", "dynamo.frontend", "--http-host", "0.0.0.0", "--http-port", "8000",
              "--discovery-backend", "file", "--request-plane", "tcp"]
    environment:
      DYN_FILE_KV: /dynamo-kv
      # Traces -> the lab's collector (Tempo/Phoenix/Langfuse), same bus name every other service uses.
      # Off until you flip it: the endpoint below is only reachable when observability/ is up.
      DYN_LOGGING_JSONL: "${DYN_LOGGING_JSONL:-false}"
      OTEL_EXPORT_ENABLED: "${OTEL_EXPORT_ENABLED:-false}"
      OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT: http://otel-collector:4317
      OTEL_SERVICE_NAME: dynamo-frontend
    volumes:
      - dynamo-kv:/dynamo-kv
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8020:8000"        # host loopback only; 8000 is taken by the vllm-* engines
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "python3 -c \"import urllib.request as u;u.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:8000/health',timeout=3)\""]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 20s
    read_only: true
    # The frontend materialises each worker's model card (tokenizer, chat template) into
    # ~/.cache/dynamo before it will list the model. read_only:true without this = an EMPTY
    # /v1/models and a WARN "creating MDC blobs dir ... Read-only file system" on repeat.
    tmpfs: [/tmp, /home/dynamo/.cache]
    pids_limit: 512

  dynamo-worker:
    <<: *common
    command: >
      python3 -m dynamo.vllm
      --model /root/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--unsloth--Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4/snapshots/16b6615af3548b88e2d8e382457bc705b00479cf
      --served-model-name unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4
      --discovery-backend file
      --request-plane tcp
      --dyn-tool-call-parser qwen3_coder
      --dyn-reasoning-parser qwen3
      --dyn-enable-structural-tag
      --max-model-len ${CTX:-262144}
      --speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":2}'
      --gpu-memory-utilization ${GPU_MEM_UTIL:-0.50}
      --kv-cache-memory-bytes ${KV_CACHE_MEMORY:-20000000000}
      --max-num-seqs ${MAX_NUM_SEQS:-64}
      --max-num-batched-tokens 8192
      --enable-chunked-prefill
      --enable-prefix-caching
    environment:
      # The image's HOME is /home/dynamo even for uid 0, so without this the flashinfer/vllm cache
      # volumes below (mounted at /root/.cache) are never used and every start recompiles.
      HOME: /root
      DYN_FILE_KV: /dynamo-kv
      DYN_SYSTEM_PORT: "8081"        # worker /metrics (+ engine metrics), scraped on the bus
      HF_HUB_OFFLINE: "1"
      TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST: "12.0"
      CUTE_DSL_ARCH: "sm_120"
      FLASHINFER_NVCC_THREADS: "2"
      NVCC_THREADS: "2"
      MAX_JOBS: "4"
      OTEL_SERVICE_NAME: dynamo-worker
    volumes:
      - dynamo-kv:/dynamo-kv
      - /srv/models/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface
      - flashinfer-cache:/root/.cache/flashinfer
      - vllm-cache:/root/.cache/vllm
    ipc: host
    deploy:
      resources:
        reservations:
          devices:
            - driver: nvidia
              device_ids: ["GPU-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001"]   # Workstation Edition, same card as vllm-qwen38
              capabilities: [gpu]
    depends_on: [dynamo-frontend]

  # CPU-only stand-in worker to prove frontend<->worker discovery + routing with NO VRAM.
  # `docker compose --profile mock up -d` — never alongside dynamo-worker (same model name).
  # --model-path is the pinned SNAPSHOT DIR, not the repo id: the shared cache's refs/main points at
  # a different revision than the pin, so the id form fails "Model snapshots ... not found in cache".
  dynamo-mocker:
    <<: *common
    profiles: [mock]
    command: ["python3", "-m", "dynamo.mocker", "--model-path",
              "/root/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--unsloth--Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4/snapshots/16b6615af3548b88e2d8e382457bc705b00479cf",
              "--model-name", "unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-NVFP4", "--discovery-backend", "file", "--request-plane", "tcp"]
    environment:
      DYN_FILE_KV: /dynamo-kv
      HF_HUB_OFFLINE: "1"
    volumes:
      - dynamo-kv:/dynamo-kv
      - /srv/models/hf:/root/.cache/huggingface:ro
    depends_on: [dynamo-frontend]

volumes:
  dynamo-kv:
  flashinfer-cache:
  vllm-cache:

networks:
  ai-lab:
    external: true

# Provider profile: the lab's LiteLLM router for Data Designer sandboxes.
# The sandbox never holds the key: OpenShell stores it in the gateway credential store and the
# supervisor injects it into requests matching these endpoints, from the listed binaries only.
# Install:  openshell profile lint -f profile-lab-router.yaml
#           openshell profile import -f profile-lab-router.yaml --global
#           LITELLM_DD_KEY=$(cat ~/.config/data-designer/litellm.key) \
#             openshell provider create --name lab-router-dd --type lab-litellm-dd
# Attach at sandbox create with --provider lab-router-dd.
id: lab-litellm-dd
display_name: Lab LiteLLM Router (Data Designer)
description: Synthetic-data generation through the local LiteLLM router (key_alias data-designer). Plaintext HTTP on the ai-lab bus; inspected and credential-rewritten by the supervisor.
category: inference
inference_capable: true

credentials:
  - name: litellm_dd_key
    description: LiteLLM virtual key (key_alias data-designer, all models, no admin)
    env_vars: [LITELLM_DD_KEY]
    required: true
    auth_style: bearer
    header_name: authorization

discovery:
  credentials: [litellm_dd_key]

endpoints:
  - host: 172.16.0.5
    port: 4000
    path: /v1/**
    protocol: rest
    enforcement: enforce
    allowed_ips:
      - 172.16.0.5/32
    rules:
      - allow:
          method: "*"
          path: "/v1/**"

binaries:
  - /usr/local/bin/python3.13

dict: Synthetic-data generation through the local LiteLLM router (key_alias data-designer). Plaintext HTTP on the ai-lab bus; inspected and credential-rewritten by the supervisor.

# ai-lab-dd — the OpenShell gateway for the Data Designer sandbox runner (and future lab runners).
#
# Topology (rootless Docker, see IMPLEMENTATION.md §3):
#   * `openshell-docker` (172.16.0.0/24) is an INTERNAL network: no route off the box. On it: the
#     gateway (static 172.16.0.2), every sandbox container, and the LiteLLM router (172.16.0.5,
#     attached by data-designer-local's ensure_gateway(); see the note at the bottom). The driver
#     pins host.openshell.internal -> 172.16.0.2 in each sandbox's /etc/hosts (config/gateway.toml).
#   * `openshell-cli` is a normal user-defined network that exists ONLY so the CLI forwarder can
#     publish 127.0.0.1:17670 (an internal network cannot publish ports). Nothing else joins it.
#   Recreate the internal network (one-time, or after `docker network rm`):
#     docker network create --internal --subnet 172.16.0.0/24 openshell-docker
#   data-designer-local refuses to run if it is not internal.
#
#   Started on demand by clients/data-designer/data-designer-local (ensure_gateway()).
#
# Auth: mTLS. The CLI connects over https with the client bundle; sandbox supervisors present
# their per-sandbox JWTs. RESIDUAL (OpenShell 0.0.77 design, cannot be changed by config): the
# Docker driver bind-mounts the SAME client cert+key the CLI uses into every sandbox container at
# /etc/openshell/tls/client/. They are root-only (0600) there and the workload runs as uid 1000
# under Landlock — verified 2026-10-24 that the workload cannot read tls.key or sandbox.jwt — so
# using them needs a root escalation inside the sandbox container first. Per-sandbox credentials
# need OIDC (no IdP in the lab) or a newer OpenShell.
#
# Pins (digest = what was scanned; bump = re-scan per clients/ADDING-PACKAGES.md, then update the
# scan record in ../README.md):
#   gateway     ghcr.io/nvidia/openshell/gateway:0.0.77 @sha256:ba6f6537…63e8
#   supervisor  ghcr.io/nvidia/openshell/supervisor:31807d68… @sha256:e796ba93…a0a0a (same 2026-07-06
#               build as the gateway; pinned in config/gateway.toml with pull policy Never)
#   forwarder   alpine/socat:1.8.0.1 @sha256:87d88ff7…99e7
name: ai-lab-dd

services:
  gateway:
    image: ghcr.io/nvidia/openshell/gateway@sha256:ba6f6537544d5dcb949ebb926cece206c01ca4546552934d91ebb9d8ea7363e8
    container_name: ai-lab-dd-gateway
    # Container root maps to host uid 1000 in rootless Docker; the image's own uid 1000 maps into
    # the subordinate range and could not read the state dir or the Docker socket. Root here means
    # "your uid", so it holds no more than you do — but it does hold the Docker socket, which is why
    # it gets no capabilities, no privilege escalation and no network route off the box.
    user: "0"
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    networks:
      openshell-docker:
        ipv4_address: 172.16.0.2
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      # The 0.0.77 Docker driver hardcodes the REAL home paths for what it bind-mounts into sandbox
      # containers (tokens + TLS under ~/.local/state/openshell, the supervisor store under
      # ~/.local/share/openshell) and the HOST daemon resolves those sources on the host fs, so the
      # gateway's state is mounted at identical paths. Both dirs are 0700.
      - /home/USER/.local/state/openshell:/home/USER/.local/state/openshell
      - /home/USER/.local/share/openshell:/home/USER/.local/share/openshell
      # The gateway's own config dir (does not touch the host's ~/.config/openshell).
      - ./config:/home/USER/.config/openshell
      # The rootless Docker socket: the gateway creates/destroys the sandbox containers.
      - /run/user/1000/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
    environment:
      OPENSHELL_COMPUTE_DRIVER: docker
      OPENSHELL_GRPC_ENDPOINT: https://host.openshell.internal:8080
      OPENSHELL_DB_URL: sqlite:/home/USER/.local/state/openshell/openshell.db
      OPENSHELL_LOCAL_TLS_DIR: /home/USER/.local/state/openshell/tls
      OPENSHELL_TLS_CERT: /home/USER/.local/state/openshell/tls/server/tls.crt
      OPENSHELL_TLS_KEY: /home/USER/.local/state/openshell/tls/server/tls.key
      OPENSHELL_TLS_CLIENT_CA: /home/USER/.local/state/openshell/tls/ca.crt
      OPENSHELL_ENABLE_MTLS_AUTH: "true"
      # OpenShell's own telemetry off (the driver passes this into every sandbox; the internal
      # network means it has nowhere to go anyway).
      OPENSHELL_TELEMETRY_ENABLED: "false"
      HOME: /home/USER
      NEMO_TELEMETRY_ENABLED: "false"

  cli-forwarder:
    image: alpine/socat@sha256:87d88ff79bf42ca723fb360e9585c40e2923a2f4df9b9d148b127568ef6b99e7
    container_name: ai-lab-dd-cli-fwd
    restart: unless-stopped
    # A fixed TCP forward and nothing else: no root, no capabilities, read-only filesystem.
    user: "65534:65534"
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true
    networks:
      # openshell-cli is the network the published port rides on (gw_priority makes it the default
      # route); openshell-docker is how it reaches the gateway.
      openshell-cli:
        gw_priority: 1
      openshell-docker: {}
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:17670:8080"
    command: "TCP-LISTEN:8080,fork,reuseaddr TCP:172.16.0.2:8080"

networks:
  openshell-docker:
    external: true
  openshell-cli:
    name: openshell-cli
    # Explicit subnet: the lab's ~50 networks have exhausted Docker's default address pools.
    # 172.16.1.0/29 sits next to openshell-docker (172.16.0.0/24) and collides with no route here.
    ipam:
      config:
        - subnet: 172.16.1.0/29

# Why the router's attachment to openshell-docker is NOT in inference/litellm/docker-compose.yml:
# an external network there would make the router (the mesh's single chokepoint) fail to start
# whenever this OpenShell network is absent. data-designer-local re-pins it before every run
# instead, and the network is internal, so the router gains no route off the box from it.

# Sandbox policy for Data Designer runs (Nemo Console / CLI: `openshell sandbox create --policy`).
# Confinement story: Landlock scopes the filesystem (workspace /work writable; the baked tool
# config /opt/dd-config read-only; system paths read-only), and the only network egress is the
# lab's LiteLLM router (172.16.0.5:4000 = litellm pinned on openshell-docker, /v1/**) for the Python interpreter data-designer actually
# connects with — enforced by the OpenShell supervisor, default-deny for everything else.
# The router credential is NOT in the sandbox: a provider profile (lab-litellm-dd) injects the
# LITELLM_DD_KEY value into approved requests; the workload sees a placeholder only.
version: 1
filesystem_policy:
  include_workdir: true
  read_only:
    - /opt/dd-config
    - /home/sandbox
    - /usr
    - /lib
    - /proc
    - /dev/urandom
  read_write:
    - /sandbox
network_policies:
  lab_router:
    endpoints:
      - host: 172.16.0.5
        port: 4000
        protocol: rest
        enforcement: enforce
        allowed_ips:
          - 172.16.0.5/32
        rules:
          - allow:
              method: "*"
              path: "/v1/**"
    binaries:
      - path: /usr/local/bin/python3.13
